Home / Languages / High Valyrian

High Valyrian

Valyrio Muño Ōreloso

Created by David J. Peterson · Game of Thrones / House of the Dragon (HBO)

Grammar Overview

  • Four grammatical genders — Lunar, Solar, Terrestrial, Aquatic — adjectives agree with noun gender. Getting gender wrong is one of the most visible errors in HV writing.
  • Eight noun cases — Nominative, Accusative, Genitive, Dative, Locative, Instrumental, Comitative, Vocative. Inflections cascade through adjectives and determiners.
  • Verb-final tendency — HV trends toward SOV order. Verbs carry full agreement for tense, mood, voice, person, and number.
  • Macron vowels carry stress — Long vowels (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū, ȳ) are prosodically stressed. These are rhythmic anchor points in the lyrics — every line lands on a macron-stressed syllable.
  • Past tense -tas / -tan — 3sg past: -tas. 1sg past: -tan. These verb endings create natural couplet rhyme in the Ozymandias lyrics.

sagon to be; to exist
notes

[C-P] Core copula. iksan = I am (1sg present); issa = it is (3sg present).

dārys king
notes

[C-P] Lunar gender. Genitive Dāryro = king's. Appears in compound zaldrīz-dārys (dragon-king).

zaldrīz dragon
notes

[C-P] Appears in compounds: zaldrīz-dārys (dragon-king, singular), zaldrīz-dārī (dragonlords, plural).

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
zaldrīz-dārys zaldrīz + dārys dragon-king
notes

[C-P] Compound: zaldrīz (dragon) + dārys (king). The statue-figure's self-description in the Ozymandias chorus. Plural zaldrīz-dārī = dragonlords.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
ñuha my (1st person singular possessive)
notes

[C-P] Agrees with noun gender/case. Ñuhī = plural form (agreeing with gaomoti = works). The possessive in the refrain: ñuhī gaomoti = my works.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
gaomagon to do; to make; to act
notes

[C-P] Gaomoti = result noun, works/deeds (plural). Central noun of the Ozymandias proclamation.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
obūlagon to behold; to look upon
notes

[C-P] obūlās = imperative = behold! The Ozymandias command. Used twice in chorus and twice in final chorus.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
pāsagon to believe; to trust; to have faith
notes

[C-P] pāsās = imperative = believe! Used ironically in the refrain: "se daor pāsās" = and believe nothing. The king commands you to believe; the desolation commands otherwise.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
se and (coordinating conjunction)
notes

[C-P] High-frequency conjunction.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
daor not; no; nothing
notes

[C-P] Core negating particle. "Brōzi daor" = no name. "Jaes daor" = no god. Extended as Daoruni (nothingness) in Verse 3 and outro.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
ondos hand
notes

[C-P] Solar gender. Instrumental ondoso = by hand. Three appearances: "valo ondoso" (by the man's hand), "Māzittio ondos" (the maker's hand), "Ondos dōron pryjattas" (the hand broke stone).

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
vala man; person
notes

[C-P] Lunar gender. Genitive valo = of the man / man's. The unnamed sculptor: "valo ondoso" = by the man's hand.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
mērī both; all; entirely
notes

[C-P] Distributive determiner. Used twice for the symmetry between sculptor and king — both reduced equally to dust.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
dōron stone
notes

[C-P] Terrestrial gender. High-frequency: in compounds (dōron-krisi), in standalone lines, and as the instrument of preservation. The stone outlasts everything.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
syt only; just; merely
notes

[C-P] Limiting particle.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
āejot now; still; yet
notes

[C-P] Temporal adverb. "Mērī jeson āejot" = both dust now. "dōron vēdes syt ziry āejot" = the stone sings of them still.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
hēnka beneath; under; only (particle with dual role)
notes

[C-P] Functions as spatial (beneath) and limiting (only) depending on context. FLAG: two uses in Mirros Naejot Daoruni — verify that both readings are documented senses.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
bē upon; on; against (postposition)
notes

[C-P/C-D] Postposition following the noun it governs. "Pryjata dōronon bē" = upon the broken stone.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
rōva great; large; powerful
notes

[C-P] Adjective with gender agreement. Rōvī = plural form. "Rōva eglie udir" = the great old speech.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
yn but; yet; however
notes

[C-P] Adversative conjunction. "Yn skoros ziry rȳbatas daor" = but no one heard them.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
skoros who; what; which (relative/interrogative)
notes

[C-P] "Yn skoros ziry rȳbatas daor" = but who heard them not = but no one heard them.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
ziry them; their; him/her (3rd person oblique)
notes

[C-P] Third-person pronoun, oblique case. Three uses in the Bridge: the stone hears them, no one else hears them, the stone sings of them still.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
rȳbagon to hear; to listen
notes

[C-P] Past form rȳbatas (3sg = heard).

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
māzigon to arrive; to come; to approach
notes

[C-P] māzitan = I came (1sg past); māzitto = agent noun: one who comes / maker; māzittī = latecomers (those who come after); māzitos = came (3sg past, the Doom arrived).

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni
umbagon to remain; to stay; to persist
notes

[C-P] umbis = 3sg present = remains. The persistence verb throughout — the broken speech remains when everything else has gone.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni

notes

[C-P] Title word and thematic core. "Mirros āena umbis" = nothing else remains. Extended as Daoruni (absolute nothingness) in Verse 3.

 [C-P] Peterson canon mirros-naejot-daoruni

notes

[C-D] "Jaes daor" = no god. The Verse 3 desolation: no name, no god, nothing.

notes

[C-P/C-D] Directional particle. "Zōbrie dōron-krisi, naejot, iōragis" = black stone-legs, before me, standing. Also: naejot māzittī = latecomers.

[C-P] urnesi = 3pl present = they see.

notes

[C-P] Root of Valar morghulis. Past form morghontas = died (3sg). "Valyria perzosa morghontas" = Valyria died by fire.

[C-P/C-D] Locative particle.

daoruni nothingness; absolute negation; the void
notes

[N] Extended form of daor with intensifying suffix -uni, creating a noun from the particle. Reifies the absence. Used as the final anaphoric refrain: "Daoruni — daoruni — daoruni." The title-adjacent word: Mirros = silence, Daoruni = the nothingness underneath it.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
dōron-krisi dōron + krisi stone-legs (compound noun)
notes

[N] dōron (stone) + krisi (legs). Shelley's "two vast and trunkless legs of stone" rendered as a High Valyrian compound. The first image the wanderer encounters across the burnt land.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
krisi legs (plural)
notes

[N] Coined for this track. No documented HV word for leg/legs. Do not confuse with Suh Ankripton kriso — coincidental phonological similarity between unrelated conlangs.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni

notes

[N] Compound: fire-element (perzys, compound form) + tegot (ground/land). The Valyrian wasteland the wanderer crosses in Verse 1. FLAG: tegon vs. tegot — Verse 3 uses tegon standalone; the compound uses tegot. Verify compounding alternation.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
tegon ground; earth; land surface
notes

[N] "Gīda tegon, gīda jeson" = level ground, level dust. FLAG: appears as tegon in Verse 3 but tegot in the compound perzys-tegot. See above.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni

notes

[N] Participial form iōragis = standing. "Zōbrie dōron-krisi, naejot, iōragis" = black stone-legs, before me, standing.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
iosre cold; frigid
notes

[N] "Laesī iosre" = eyes cold. The cold gaze of the statue — command preserved in stone.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
pryjagon to break; to shatter; to fracture
notes

[N] High-frequency. Forms: pryjata (broken, adjective), pryjattas (broke, 3sg past), pryjatī (broken, plural adjective). The central action-state of the track: what is broken is what endures.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni

notes

[N] Past form rāeltas = kept/preserved (3sg). The stone preserves what maker and king could not.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
hōzie swollen; bloated; puffed with pride
notes

[N] "Dāryro hōzie prūmia jesor issa" = the king's swollen heart is dust. The Shelley-original sense of pride so inflated it deformed the face it was carved on.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
prūmia heart (as organ and seat of pride)
notes

[N] "Dāryro hōzie prūmia" = the king's swollen heart.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
eglie old; ancient; from long ago
notes

[N] "Rōva eglie udir" = the great old speech. The inscription is ancient — it predates the Doom, predates the wanderer, outlasts both.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
udir speech; tongue; language; inscription
notes

[N] The central artifact of the track: what remains on the stone is language. "Rōva eglie udir umbis" = the great old speech remains. "Valyrīho udir" = Valyria's tongue. "Zaldrīz-dārī udiroso arghugar" = the dragonlords shouted in their tongue.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
qogror people; folk; a civilization
notes

[N] "Qogror perzys-māzitto" = the fire-bringer people. Identifies the Valyrians through their defining attribute without using franchise-specific terms.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
perzys-māzitto perzo + māzitto fire-bringers; people of fire
notes

[N] Compound: fire-element (perzys) + māzitto (one who comes/brings). Used in apposition: "qogror perzys-māzitto" = the fire-bringer people.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
gīda level; flat; featureless
notes

[N] "Gīda tegon, gīda jeson" = level ground, level dust. The anaphoric repetition mirrors the desolate sameness of the wasteland.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni

notes

[N] "Brōzi daor" = no name. FLAG: unclear whether brōzi is nominative or a declined form. Treat as canonical until base form is confirmed.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
āena else; other; beyond
notes

[N/C-D] "Mirros āena umbis" = nothing else remains.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
vējes the Doom; catastrophic end; destruction
notes

[N] The Valyrian Doom as named event. "Vējes māzitos" = the Doom came. Recognizable to franchise readers; legible from context to others.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
arghugon to shout; to cry out
notes

[N] Past form arghugar = shouted (3pl). "Zaldrīz-dārī udiroso arghugar" = the dragonlords shouted in their tongue. The futile final cry before the Doom silenced them.

 [N] New construction mirros-naejot-daoruni
vēdegon to sing; to resound; to carry sound
notes

[N] vēdes = sings (3sg present). "Dōron vēdes syt ziry āejot" = the stone sings of them still. The stone as passive repository — carrying the sound of the past without choosing to.

New Constructions

Words coined for Borrowed Tongues releases. Each entry documents the derivation reasoning so the logic is transparent and reviewable.

nothingness; absolute negation; the void

[N] Extended form of daor with intensifying suffix -uni, creating a noun from the particle. Reifies the absence. Used as the final anaphoric refrain: "Daoruni — daoruni — daoruni." The title-adjacent word: Mirros = silence, Daoruni = the nothingness underneath it.
